provider: OVHcloud Public Cloud Swift Cloud Archive containers
category: OpenStack Swift cold archive, legacy Public Cloud class

free_tier.stated: No free tier: Cloud Archive is billed from the first GB at USD 0.0000033 per GB-hour (about USD 0.002409 per GB-month), plus USD 0.011 per GB of incoming public traffic
free_tier.notes: billed per GiB-hour; the monthly figure is the hourly price x 730 hours

per_object_cap.stated: 5368709122 bytes (5 GB) for a normal object; a larger object is uploaded in segments of up to that size
per_object_cap.notes: a segmented large object has no total size stated on the page read

retention.stated: unlimited volume and time: data is kept until deleted; a retrieval request, the unfreeze, is required before an archived object can be read, and it takes a delay
retention.notes: unverified: no minimum storage duration is stated on the pages read

egress.terms: Incoming public traffic costs USD 0.011 per GB; internal traffic and outgoing public traffic are free; an object must be unfrozen before it is read
egress.price_per_tb: USD 11 per TB of incoming public traffic (USD 0.011 per GB x 1000 GB per TB)

interface_detail: OpenStack Swift API, with SFTP and SCP clients for the download
tooling: python-swiftclient, Cyberduck, a Swift, SFTP or SCP client
chaining: an archive tier for cold data; an object is unfrozen, then downloaded through a Swift, SFTP or SCP client

limits.value: 5368709122 bytes (5 GB) per normal object; larger objects use segments

limits_note: Legacy cold class: a retrieval request is required and delays reading; the US price list shows USD 0.0121 per GB for incoming public traffic against USD 0.011 on the international list
binding_note: none: storage has no stated cap; a normal object is limited to 5 GB with larger objects stored as segments, and reads wait on an unfreeze request

identity_cost.detail: an email address validated by a one-time code, the country of tax residence, and a valid payment method on the account before the first Public Cloud project

reliability_note: no availability SLA figure is stated on the pages read: unverified; the class holds cold data behind a retrieval request
confidence_note: documented: the international price list, the storage classes pages, the endpoints page and the technical limits page were read and quoted on 2026-11-03; a read timed from a bucket would make it measured

evidence.proved: Cloud Archive costs USD 0.0000033 per GB-hour, about USD 0.002409 per GB-month, with USD 0.011 per GB of incoming public traffic and free internal and outgoing traffic

evidence.quote: For optimal readability, the price is displayed as GB/month – but since there are 730 hours in an average month, the invoicing granularity is GB/hour.
evidence.proved: Cloud Archive is invoiced per GB-hour and the monthly figure assumes 730 hours
the US price list charges USD 0.0121 per GB of incoming public traffic for Cloud Archive, against USD 0.011 on the international list

evidence.quote: The Cloud Archive (Swift) storage class offers a storage service for long-term data retention for business needs or other obligations. Adapted to suit this use case, the service offers low storage costs and several minutes of latency for data recovery. The solution is accessible via a Swift API.
evidence.proved: Cloud Archive is a Swift-API cold class with several minutes of latency to recover data

evidence.quote: Since cold storage data is supposed to be rarely accessed, a retrieval request is required, implying a delay prior to recovering the data.
evidence.proved: reading an archived object needs a retrieval request and a delay

evidence.quote: The Swift storage classes are from older generations and no longer benefit from further developments.
evidence.proved: the Swift classes are legacy and receive no further development
Cloud Archive is offered in Strasbourg, Gravelines, London, Frankfurt and Warsaw
the Cloud Archive Swift maximum normal object is 5368709122 bytes

evidence.proved: a valid payment method is required on the account before the first Public Cloud project

evidence.quote: After you submit this form, a one-time code will be sent to the email address you entered.
